title: Treatment, stress and health problems
summary: Biological and psychological treatments for depression, how stress affects health, and explaining and preventing a health problem such as obesity.

keyterms.definition: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor: an antidepressant that blocks reuptake of serotonin, e.g. fluoxetine.
A therapy that challenges negative thoughts and changes behaviour patterns.
An inactive treatment used as a control to separate real drug effects from expectation.
Participants are randomly allocated to treatment or control conditions to test effectiveness.
A response that occurs when demands are perceived to exceed one's ability to cope.
Selye's model of the stress response: alarm, resistance and exhaustion.
A stress hormone that releases energy but, when chronically high, suppresses the immune system.
Excess body fat, usually defined as a BMI of 30 or more in adults.
A model predicting health behaviour from perceived susceptibility, severity, benefits, barriers and cues to action.

questions.prompt: In the TADS study (March et al., 2004) of adolescents with depression, which condition had the highest response rate?
questions.explanation: The combination did best, suggesting biological and psychological treatments can complement each other.

questions.prompt: Kirsch et al. (2008) analysed antidepressant trial data. They concluded that the difference between drug and placebo was:
options: Small, except for the most severely depressed
questions.explanation: This raised questions about how much benefit comes from expectation.

questions.statement: SSRIs work by blocking the reuptake of serotonin, leaving more in the synapse.
questions.explanation: This increases serotonin availability, though mood improvement usually takes weeks.

questions.statement: CBT focuses mainly on uncovering unconscious childhood conflicts.
questions.explanation: CBT targets current thoughts and behaviours; that description fits psychodynamic therapy.

questions.text: An inactive pill used as a control in drug trials is a ___.
questions.explanation: Placebo control separates drug effects from expectancy effects.

questions.text: DeRubeis et al. (2005) found CBT was as effective as ___ for moderate to severe depression at 16 weeks.
questions.explanation: Both produced similar response rates in this trial.

questions.prompt: Match each treatment to an evaluation point.
questions.explanation: No single treatment suits everyone.

questions.prompt: Why are double-blind RCTs important in treatment research?
options: They reduce expectation effects from both patients and researchers
They remove the need for consent
questions.explanation: Blinding protects against participant and researcher bias.

questions.prompt: An ethical issue in giving a placebo to depressed participants is:
options: They may be denied effective treatment while suicidal risk exists
questions.explanation: Researchers must monitor risk and allow withdrawal.

questions.prompt: Order the main stages of CBT for depression.
items: Assessment and building a working relationship
questions.explanation: CBT is structured and time-limited.

questions.prompt: Kiecolt-Glaser et al. (1995) compared wound healing in caregivers of relatives with dementia and controls. Caregivers' wounds:
questions.explanation: Chronic stress was linked to slower healing (about 9 days, or 24%, longer), showing an effect on the immune system.

questions.prompt: In Selye's general adaptation syndrome, which stage follows prolonged exposure to a stressor?
questions.explanation: After alarm and resistance, resources are depleted in the exhaustion stage, increasing illness risk.

questions.statement: Kiecolt-Glaser et al. (1995) was a quasi-experiment because caregiver status was not randomly allocated.
questions.explanation: Other differences between groups could have contributed.

questions.statement: Stunkard et al. (1986) found adoptees' BMI was more strongly related to their adoptive parents' BMI than to their biological parents'.
questions.explanation: BMI was related to biological parents, suggesting a genetic influence on obesity.

questions.text: The stress hormone that suppresses the immune system when chronically high is ___.
questions.explanation: Long-term cortisol release links stress to illness.

questions.text: In the health belief model, a reminder text from a doctor is a cue to ___.
questions.explanation: Cues to action trigger health behaviour.

questions.prompt: Match each GAS stage to its description.
questions.explanation: Selye based his model partly on animal research.

questions.prompt: Which is a sociocultural factor in obesity?
options: Norms around food portions and observing family eating habits
questions.explanation: Social learning and cultural norms shape eating behaviour.

questions.prompt: A health campaign shows how serious type 2 diabetes is. Which HBM factor does it target?
questions.explanation: Increasing perceived severity is predicted to increase health behaviour.

questions.prompt: Order the stages of Selye's general adaptation syndrome.
questions.explanation: Prolonged stress leads to exhaustion.
